Apt Maintenance Redesign

As part of competitor analysis, I documented a parallel maintenance workflow from another apartment app through user screen recordings. Comparing ticket submission and history review flows revealed alternative approaches to navigation, feedback, and system transparency.
Background

Based on usability testing, I identified several friction points in the maintenance request workflow. These insights informed a set of targeted design decisions aimed at improving clarity, reducing cognitive load, and creating a more guided experience.

Improved visibility of updates and maintenance notes

In the summer of 2025, a severe tornado struck St. Louis, causing widespread damage across the city. My apartment building, Expo at Forest Park, sat near the center of the storm and was heavily affected. In the months that followed, residents experienced multiple issues including broken windows, leaking roofs, inconsistent water service, and long periods without air conditioning.
Inadequate maintenance services damage user trust and bring long-term risks to property management.
Insights

Instead of hard-coding every input field, I structured the code using reusable components. This aligns the frontend architecture with Figma's component system, ensuring visual consistency and reducing engineering debt.

Surveyed 30 residents to quantify maintenance habits and pain points.
The maintenance section of the App felt confusing and difficult to use.

To evaluate usability, I tested the Expo maintenance workflow with three users who had no prior experience. Across all sessions, users hesitated and expressed uncertainty at multiple steps, revealing gaps in clarity, navigation, and system feedback. These observations informed the need for a more guided and intuitive workflow design.
